_: SEC-5 justified exceptions for tools/secret-scan.mjs. Each entry is a (file, key) pair, never a whole file, because allowlisting a file pre-authorizes every secret a later edit pastes into it. 'why' is mandatory and is the review surface: an entry whose reason does not survive reading is an entry to delete, not to keep. An entry matching nothing fails the scan, so this list cannot silently outlive what it exempts.

allow.why: Test fixtures, not secrets: the CFG-1 settings tests assert that a secret-shaped value resolves from the secrets source and never from committed configuration, so they must construct values of that shape to have anything to assert about. 'sk-live-oops' is the negative control, named to read as the mistake it stands in for.

The SEC-4 verification tests both mint and verify with this phrase, so it is a fixture and not a credential: no shipped code path signs or verifies with it and no deployed process can reach it. Building tokens is the only way to prove a verifier, because unlike the sibling this edition has no configuration object to read the validation back off, and E-88 measured what proving by configuration alone costs: five of the sibling's seven validation properties can be set permissive with all 261 tests green, for want of a violating input to send.
